data.name: Vrindavan
data.gender_notes: Vrindavan is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vrindavan is a holy town in India, where Lord Krishna is believed to have spent his childhood. The name signifies 'forest of Tulsi' in Sanskrit. The name Vrindavan carries the meaning “Forest of Tulsi” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vrindavan usually hope their child will grow to embody forest of tulsi and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine love and spiritual growth.
data.etymology: Vrindavan belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Forest of Tulsi.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vrindavan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Vrindavan is a place of great cultural significance for Hindus, as it is considered one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites. It is the location of numerous ancient temples and is famous for its vibrant festivals and rich tradition of devotional music, dance, and literature.
data.spiritual_significance: Vrindavan holds deep spiritual significance for Hindus and is considered a place where one can attain spiritual growth and enlightenment. It is believed that Lord Krishna chose this place to dwell among the people and share his divine love and teachings. The name 'Vrindavan', or the 'forest of Tulsi', represents the spiritual connection between the divine and the natural world and is a reminder of the importance of devotion and love in one's spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vrindavan is a sacred city in India, associated with Lord Krishna and the divine pastimes that took place there. It symbolizes the eternal abode of love and devotion, where the soul finds its ultimate refuge in the loving embrace of the divine.

vedic_reference.note: Vrinda refers to the sacred Tulsi (Basil) plant, and vana means forest or grove. This name appears in the Bhagavata Purana and is associated with Lord Krishna's childhood pastimes.

historical_references.reference: Vrindavan is believed to have been the place where Lord Krishna spent his childhood days, playing and frolicking with the cowherd boys and the gopis (milkmaids) in the forests of Vrindavan. This period is referred to as 'Vrindavana-lila' in Hindu mythology.

Vrindavan is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Bhagavad Purana and the Mahabharata. It is described as a place of spiritual significance and pilgrimage for devotees of Lord Krishna.
historical_references.time_period: circa 1000 BC - 500 AD (Vedic and medieval periods)
